rationale: Verbal noun from ⲱⲙⲥ̄ 'submerge, dive' (already in glossary as ⲁⲱⲙⲥ̄). Used here of the First Man's primordial submergence in the Deep of Darkness — the cosmogonic moment of his being engulfed by the matter he descended to combat. Receives ϫⲓ ('receive') as its verb: 'received submergence.'

Standard Coptic noun 'recompense, exchange-gift, reciprocation' (= Sahidic ⲧⲱⲱⲃⲉ). Used here in disciples' rhetorical question: who has power to grasp the apostle 'in recompense for' (ⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲃ̄ⲓⲱ ⲙ̄-) the favor he has done? Captures the formal exchange-economy of teacher-disciple gratitude.
Compound: ⲡⲱϩ 'reach' + ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ 'to (one's) hand.' Idiom for what 'falls to one's lot, comes within one's grasp.' Lines 9-10: 'this favor alone has reached unto our hand — to grasp you.'
Already in glossary; reaffirmed here as the apostle's standard teaching-formula opening expositions. Lyc. ⲱⲱⲡⲉ = ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become.' The construction is split across lines 16-17 ⲱⲱ-ⲡⲉ.

Technical Manichaean cosmological-eschatological term for three primordial moments of cosmic activity, paired antithetically with 'the two deaths.' This kephalaion (39) is dedicated to enumerating them. First Day = First Man's descent and rescue (this page); subsequent Days follow.

Manichaean cosmological term paired with the three Great Days. Standard dualistic pair: the death of light-substance (its captivity in matter) and the death of the wicked (their final binding in the bōlos). Title-element of K.39.
Variant of ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲙ̄ⲫⲟⲟⲩⲉ already in glossary. The day-ship = sun-ship in which the Third Ambassador becomes seated to refine the captive light. Standard Manichaean cosmological vessel.
